claims.text: A nanocrystalline RHEA interlayer between W and CuCrZr will enhance interfacial bonding.
A nanocrystalline RHEA interlayer between W and CuCrZr will enhance thermal-shock resistance.
Direct W-to-CuCrZr bonding tends to create a brittle interfacial zone.
W and CuCrZr have mismatched thermal expansion relevant to degradation of their bonded interface.
Direct W/CuCrZr interfaces are particularly susceptible to irradiation-induced defects.
The proposed intervention is to introduce a tailored nanocrystalline RHEA thin interlayer between W and CuCrZr.
The proposed interlayer is intended to operate under high thermal gradients and neutron or ion irradiation representative of fusion environments.
A nanocrystalline RHEA interlayer will create coherent interfaces in the W/RHEA/CuCrZr structure.
The proposed coherent interfaces will accommodate thermal-expansion mismatch.
A nanocrystalline RHEA microstructure can reduce irradiation-induced defect accumulation.
Nanocrystalline RHEAs can exhibit radiation resistance under heavy-ion, dual-beam, and helium-implantation exposure.
The RHEA interlayer will mitigate thermal and mechanical stresses at the W/CuCrZr interface.
The RHEA interlayer will improve mechanical coupling at the W/CuCrZr interface.
The RHEA interlayer will reduce the formation and evolution of irradiation-induced defects.
The W/RHEA/CuCrZr interfacial region will have greater durability than a directly bonded W/CuCrZr interface.
The W/RHEA/CuCrZr structure will have better interfacial thermal and mechanical performance than directly bonded W/CuCrZr.
Existing W/CuCrZr bonds degrade under extreme irradiation and thermal cycling, reducing performance and reliability.
The cited nanocrystalline RHEA exhibited high thermal stability under the assessed extreme environments.
The exact interlayer composition and its long-term stability under a fusion-neutron spectrum remain undetermined.
Actual-reactor validation and composition optimization are still required before the proposed interlayer can be established.
